messages:
morgan: taking primary for the next 4h — quick snapshot: no open P1s, p99 inference latency ~220ms, token rate steady. leaving a short TL;DR runbook list before I head into the bridge: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/oncall-quick-checklist, https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/kvcache-troubleshoot. ping me if anything spikes :wave:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: pg-1234 (hosted-api) — elevated request latency detected for model-a variant. Severity: P2 — 1 trigger at 1765347905. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/pg-1234
jamal: on secondary. seeing the same spike on the metrics dash. any initial customer-impact flags? which routes affected?
morgan: quick look — error rate hasn't jumped yet, just latency. affected route: /v1/generate?model=model-a. likely kvcache thrash (recent traffic pattern change). starting with safe actions: prefix cache probe, then small-scale routing to model-a-quant if needed.
tara: if you want the probe command: ```sh
# run on ops bastion
curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" https://ops-api.internal/v1/kvcache/probe -d '{"pool":"model-a","prefix":"/v1/generate"}'
``` keep an eye on KV hit ratio in the dash for 2 min. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
alex: note — prefix flush/eviction can increase cpu for a short window. if you do eviction, be ready to route traffic to fallback. fallback command (manual): ```json
{ "route": "/v1/generate", "target": "model-a-quant", "weight": 20 }
``` POST to https://router.internal/shift-route — use only <30% initially.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager escalated: pg-1234 now P1 — multiple triggers and customer-affecting requests reported via telemetry at 1765348120.
jamal: ok escalated. recommend next steps: 1) prefix probe 2) if no improvement in 90s, route 20% traffic to model-a-quant 3) prepare rolling restart of model-a pool as last resort.
morgan: doing prefix probe now (running the curl). tagging runbooks: kvcache probe + fallback routing + rollout: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/kvcache-probe, https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/routing-fallbacks, https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/rollout-safe-restart
sophie: quick handoff checklist we should keep in this thread for whoever picks up: - primary_status: active incident (P1) - secondary_contact: @jamal - sla_impact: potential customer p99 > target - mitigation_progress: kvcache probe running - next_steps: route fallback if p99 not improved in 90s, prepare restart - bridge: dial +1-555-0112 code 8342
tara: if routing needed, use the router dry-run first to confirm config: ```sh
curl -XPOST https://router.internal/dryrun -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","target":"model-a-quant","weight":20}'
``` returns a simulation. then POST to /apply.
alex: if fallback applied and latency still high, do rolling restart of pods (one at a time): ```sh
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/model-a-serving --record
# verify ready pods <-> stable error rate
``` expect ~2-3 min per pod.
morgan: update: probe returned cache hit ratio drop, eviction started (ops-api returned 202). watching metrics now. if p99 drops under 300ms in next 60s i'll keep watching, otherwise will apply 20% route. calling bridge in 2.
incident-bot: bridge created: https://meet.redwood.ai/bridge/1765347890 — dial +1-555-0112 code 8342.
morgan: cache eviction trick worked — p99 dropped from 760ms -> 180ms over 90s. no routing required. leaving notes: eviction executed via ops-api, no restart, no rollback. adding incident tags and closing escalation. please keep monitoring for 15m. :white_check_mark:
